First, understand the idea

A simple rule makes the rest much easier.

THE BASICS

What are modal verbs?

Modal verbs are helping verbs. They tell us whether something is possible, allowed, necessary, advisable, or expected. They add meaning to the main verb.

Subject + modal + base verb

Examples: I can swim. · You should rest. · It might rain.

ما هي الأفعال المساعدة (Modal Verbs)؟

هي أفعال مساعدة توضّح معنى الفعل الأساسي؛ مثل القدرة أو الاحتمال أو الإذن أو النصيحة أو الضرورة.

الفاعل + الفعل المساعد + الفعل الأساسي

أمثلة: I can swim. (أستطيع السباحة) · You should rest. (ينبغي أن ترتاح)

The golden rule

After can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, and must, use the base form of the verb — without “to”, “-s”, or “-ed”.

She can swim. ✓She can swims. ✗She can to swim. ✗

13 USEFUL FORMS

How do we use them?

Three sentence patterns you will use every day.

1. Positive sentence

Subject + modal + verb

I can speak English.

I have the ability to speak English.

2. Negative sentence

Subject + modal + not + verb

You should not worry.

Short form: You shouldn't worry.

3. Question

Modal + subject + verb?

Could you help me?

We put the modal verb before the subject.

Watch out!

Does she can swim? ✗

Can she swim? ✓

Do not add do/does to form a question with a modal verb.

Quick guide: similar, but different

These pairs are easy to confuse. Notice the difference.

WordMain ideaExampleArabic
CanAbility / informal permissionI can drive.أستطيع القيادة.
CouldPast ability / polite request / possibilityCould you help me?هل يمكنك مساعدتي؟ (بأسلوب مهذب)
MayMay I come in?هل تسمح لي بالدخول؟
MightIt might snow.قد تتساقط الثلوج.
MustYou must wear a seat belt.يجب أن تضع حزام الأمان.
ShouldYou should sleep early.ينبغي أن تنام مبكرًا.
Mustn'tYou mustn't touch that.ممنوع أن تلمس ذلك.
Don't have toYou don't have to come.ليس من الضروري أن تأتي.

Mustn't ≠ Don't have to

You mustn't go. = You are not allowed to go.

لا يُسمح لك بالذهاب.

You don't have to go. = It is not necessary.

ليس من الضروري أن تذهب، لكن يمكنك ذلك.

ملاحظات مهمة

  • Ought to تعني غالبًا «ينبغي»، ويأتي بعدها to ثم الفعل الأساسي: You ought to apologize.
  • Have to وneed to تعبّران عن الضرورة، لكنهما ليستا من الأفعال المساعدة الناقصة نفسها؛ تتغير صياغتهما مع الفاعل والزمن.
  • Shall تُستخدم للاقتراح أو العرض، خصوصًا مع I وwe: Shall we start?
